title: Who Survives Depends on Existing Variation

scenes.tts: A hundred years ago, American chestnut trees were common in parts of Virginia's Blue Ridge Mountains. Then a fungus arrived from Asia. By about nineteen fifty, it had killed billions of these trees. Yet small sprouts still grow from old chestnut roots. Why do some species survive big changes, while others disappear?
scenes.visual: A row of chestnut trees; a red fungus arrives and the trunks go grey; small green sprouts rise at the roots; the essential question appears.

By about 1950, it had killed billions of these trees. Yet small sprouts still grow from old chestnut roots. Why do some species survive big changes, while others disappear?

scenes.tts: When an environment changes, members of a population do not share one fate. Some survive and reproduce. Some migrate, which means they move to a new place. Some die. A species is extinct when no living members are left anywhere. Vanishing from one forest is not extinction.
scenes.visual: A population box of six dots splits into three lanes: survive and reproduce, migrate, die; then two panels contrast gone from one forest with extinct.
scenes.narration: When an environment changes, members of a population do not share one fate. Some survive and reproduce. Some migrate, which means they move to a new place. Some die. A species is extinct when no living members are left anywhere. Vanishing from one forest is not extinction.

scenes.tts: Here are four changes that challenge populations today. Habitat loss is the destruction of the place where an organism lives. Pollution is harmful material added to air, water or soil. Climate change is a long shift in the usual weather of a region. An invasive species is a living thing brought to a new place, where it spreads and causes harm. The chestnut blight fungus is one.
scenes.visual: Four panels build one by one: a habitat shrinking, material added to water, a weather range sliding warmer, an invader spreading; the invader panel is tagged chestnut blight fungus.
scenes.narration: Here are four changes that challenge populations today. Habitat loss is the destruction of the place where an organism lives. Pollution is harmful material added to air, water or soil. Climate change is a long shift in the usual weather of a region. An invasive species is a living thing brought to a new place, where it spreads and causes harm. The chestnut blight fungus is one.

scenes.tts: Genetic variation means inherited differences among members of a population. Resistance is the ability to hold off a disease better than others can. When a new disease arrives, a population with more variation is more likely to have some members that resist it. Those members survive and pass their traits to their offspring.
scenes.visual: Eight members with resistance bars of different heights; a disease sweeps in; members with tall bars stay, the rest fade; offspring with tall bars appear.
scenes.narration: Genetic variation means inherited differences among members of a population. Resistance is the ability to hold off a disease better than others can. When a new disease arrives, a population with more variation is more likely to have some members that resist it. Those members survive and pass their traits to their offspring.

scenes.tts: Variation does not promise survival. When a change comes fast, the helpful trait usually has to be there already. American chestnuts had very little resistance to this fungus, so almost all the big trees died. The fungus can kill the trunk above the ground, but the roots, safe in the soil, often live and send up new sprouts. The new sprouts get infected and die back.
scenes.visual: A chestnut population with only short resistance bars meets the fungus and fades; then one tree: trunk dies above ground, roots live, a sprout grows and is infected.

scenes.tts: A few survivors do not make a species safe. So why do some species survive big changes, while others disappear? They are more likely to survive when some members already carry a helpful trait, and those members reproduce. If no member can survive the change, the species may become extinct.
scenes.visual: Two-part answer: survivors must reproduce; then the question is answered in two lines: helpful trait already present plus reproduction, versus none can survive and the species may become extinct.
